config.title: Anchor positioning

intro.title: Anchor positioning
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple tooltip that appears next to a button when you hover over it. You will learn how to use CSS anchor positioning to precisely place one element relative to another. The main technologies involved are CSS custom properties and the anchor() function. This beginner-friendly lesson will show you how to create dynamic, position-aware UI components without JavaScript.
intro.usecase: Anchor positioning is essential for creating precise, dynamic UI elements that need to maintain spatial relationships with other components. In real applications, you'll use this for tooltips that follow cursor position, dropdown menus that align perfectly with their trigger buttons, and contextual help panels that attach to specific form fields. Developers implement anchor positioning in dashboards for floating action buttons that stay fixed relative to data tables, and in e-commerce sites for shopping cart previews that appear near the cart icon. This technique ensures UI elements remain visually connected to their reference points regardless of screen size or scrolling behavior.

objectives: Implement anchor positioning to attach an element to a specific target on the page
Configure anchor positioning properties to control element placement relative to its anchor
Apply fallback positioning strategies when anchor elements are not visible
Construct position-try options to specify alternative placement rules
Manipulate anchor positioning to create dynamic UI components that adjust to viewport changes
Initialize anchor positioning with JavaScript to enable interactive positioning behavior

steps.title: Create a basic HTML structure with anchor and popup elements
steps.instruction: Create an HTML file with a button as the anchor element and a div as the popup element.
steps.hint: Start by writing the HTML structure. Use a <button> for the anchor and a <div> for the popup.
steps.analogousExample: Popup content
steps.seedCode: <!-- Create a button as the anchor element and a div as the popup element -->
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have an HTML file with a button and a div, ready for anchor positioning.
successCriteria: The HTML file contains a button element and a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you have both a button and a div in your HTML.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check your HTML. You need a button and a div element for anchor positioning.

steps.title: Style the anchor element with basic positioning
steps.instruction: Add CSS to give the anchor button position: relative and basic styling like background color and padding.
steps.hint: Use the button selector to apply CSS properties. Set position: relative to establish a positioning context for the popup.
steps.seedCode:
<!-- Create a button as the anchor element and a div as the popup element -->

/* Add your CSS for the anchor button here */
steps.expectedOutcome: The anchor button will have position: relative and visible styling like a blue background.
successCriteria: The CSS includes a button selector with position: relative and at least one other styling property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some styling, but make sure to include position: relative on the button.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS doesn't yet style the anchor button with position: relative. Try adding a button selector with position: relative and some basic styling.

steps.title: Style the popup element with absolute positioning
steps.instruction: Add CSS to position the popup element absolutely with top and left properties relative to the anchor button.
steps.hint: Use position: absolute on the popup element and set top and left values to position it relative to its positioned ancestor (the anchor button).
steps.seedCode:
<!-- Create a button as the anchor element and a div as the popup element -->

/* Add your CSS for the anchor button here */

/* Add CSS for the popup element here */
steps.expectedOutcome: The popup element will be positioned absolutely relative to the anchor button using top and left properties.
successCriteria: The popup element has position: absolute with top and left properties defined.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've added position: absolute and both top and left properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added CSS for the popup element with position: absolute and top/left positioning.

steps.title: Introduce the anchor() function for positioning
steps.instruction: Replace the absolute positioning values for the popup element with the anchor() function to position it relative to the anchor button.
steps.hint: Use the anchor() function with the anchor element's name and specify positioning values like 'top', 'bottom', 'left', or 'right'.
steps.seedCode:
<!-- Create a button as the anchor element and a div as the popup element -->

/* Add your CSS for the anchor button here */

/* Add CSS for the popup element here */
.popup {
  position: absolute;
  top: 0;
  left: 0;
}
steps.expectedOutcome: The popup element will be positioned using the anchor() function instead of fixed absolute values.
successCriteria: The popup element's CSS includes the anchor() function for positioning.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to replace the absolute positioning values with the anchor() function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The popup element should use the anchor() function for positioning. Check the syntax and try again.

steps.title: Set anchor positioning with position-anchor property
steps.instruction: Add the position-anchor property to the .popup class to reference the anchor element. Use the value --anchor-button to link it to the anchor element's CSS custom property.
steps.hint: The position-anchor property connects the popup to the anchor element. Use the syntax: position-anchor: --anchor-button;
steps.seedCode:
<!-- Create a button as the anchor element and a div as the popup element -->

/* Add your CSS for the anchor button here */

/* Add CSS for the popup element here */
.popup {
  position: absolute;
  top: 0;
  left: 0;
  /* Add position-anchor property here */
}
steps.expectedOutcome: The popup element will now be linked to the anchor element via the position-anchor property, establishing the positioning relationship.
successCriteria: The .popup class includes the position-anchor property with the value --anchor-button.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added the position-anchor property with the correct value --anchor-button to the .popup class.
steps.feedbackWrong: The position-anchor property is missing or incorrect. Add position-anchor: --anchor-button; to the .popup class to link it to the anchor element.

steps.title: Position the popup relative to anchor edges
steps.instruction: In the .popup rule, replace the existing top and left values with anchor() functions to position the popup relative to the anchor's top and right edges. Use anchor(top) for top and anchor(right) for left.
steps.hint: The anchor() function takes an edge value like 'top' or 'right' to position relative to that side of the anchor element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The popup will be positioned relative to the anchor's top and right edges instead of the viewport origin.
successCriteria: The .popup rule uses anchor(top) for the top property and anchor(right) for the left property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using anchor(top) for top and anchor(right) for left in the .popup rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The popup should be positioned using anchor() functions with edge values. Check that you're using anchor(top) for top and anchor(right) for left.

steps.title: Add offset positioning with anchor-size()
steps.instruction: In the .popup rule, use the anchor-size() function to offset the popup by the anchor's width and height.
steps.hint: The anchor-size() function returns the dimensions of the anchor element. Use it with calc() to adjust the top and left values.
steps.expectedOutcome: The popup will be positioned relative to the anchor's dimensions, offset by its width and height.
successCriteria: The .popup rule includes anchor-size() in the top and left properties to offset by the anchor's width and height.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to use anchor-size() in both top and left properties for proper offset.
steps.feedbackWrong: The offset isn't applied correctly. Use anchor-size() with calc() to adjust top and left based on anchor dimensions.

steps.title: Implement fallback positioning for browser support
steps.instruction: Wrap the existing anchor positioning styles for the .popup class in an @supports rule and provide absolute positioning fallback styles outside the rule.
steps.hint: Use @supports (anchor-name: --anchor) to detect browser support for anchor positioning. Place the anchor positioning styles inside this rule, and keep the basic absolute positioning styles outside as fallback.
steps.expectedOutcome: The popup will use anchor positioning in supporting browsers and fall back to basic absolute positioning in older browsers.
successCriteria: The .popup styles include an @supports rule with anchor positioning properties, and basic absolute positioning remains as fallback.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to wrap only the anchor positioning styles (like position-anchor and anchor-size) inside the @supports rule, and keep the basic absolute positioning outside as fallback.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the structure: you need to use @supports (anchor-name: --anchor) to wrap the anchor positioning styles, while keeping the basic absolute positioning styles outside this rule.

steps.title: Add interactive positioning with :hover
steps.instruction: Add a :hover pseudo-class to the anchor button to show the popup when hovering over the anchor.
steps.hint: Use the anchor button's class or element selector followed by :hover, then target the .popup element to change its display or visibility.
steps.expectedOutcome: The popup appears when the user hovers over the anchor button.
successCriteria: A :hover pseudo-class is added to the anchor button selector, targeting the .popup element to change its display or visibility property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a :hover selector, but make sure it targets the .popup element to change its display or visibility.
steps.feedbackWrong: The :hover pseudo-class is missing or not correctly targeting the popup element.

steps.title: Create multiple anchored elements with different positions
steps.instruction: Add a second anchor button and popup pair with different anchor positioning values (e.g., position the popup to the right of the anchor).
steps.hint: Duplicate the existing anchor and popup HTML structure, then modify the CSS selectors and anchor positioning values for the new pair.
steps.expectedOutcome: The page will display two separate anchor/popup pairs, with the second popup positioned differently relative to its anchor (e.g., to the right).
successCriteria: A second anchor button and popup element are added with distinct CSS selectors and different anchor positioning values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a second anchor/popup pair, but the positioning values might not be different from the first pair. Ensure the new popup uses distinct anchor positioning (e.g., to the right).
steps.feedbackWrong: The second anchor/popup pair is missing or doesn't have different positioning. Add a new anchor button and popup with unique CSS selectors and modify the anchor positioning values.
